objective: Add provider-neutral fail-closed admission for reversible scaffold-only self-improvement candidates using baseline/candidate digests, held-out evaluation evidence, quality/safety/regression thresholds, approval, canary, expiry, generation, ABI, and rollback controls without modifying code, weights, privileged kernel, or production policy.

research_inputs.finding: Guardrails validate inputs, outputs, and tool behavior; human review pauses before side effects; approval state is resumable; sensitive actions should fail closed when review is unavailable.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Candidate admission requires explicit approval, and canary verification is separate from admission. The ledger emits no deployment action and rejects rollback-requested or incomplete canaries.

research_inputs.finding: Blocking guardrails can prevent expensive or side-effecting execution from starting; tool guardrails are needed at each custom tool boundary; tripwires halt execution and preserve relevant state without accepting a rejected output.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The contract separates candidate evidence admission from canary verification, requires a bounded scaffold component, and explicitly records that no code, weights, policy, model, or tool execution occurred.

research_inputs.finding: Self-improving agents can modify foundation models or operational scaffolds such as prompts, memory, tools, and control logic; update signals, update substrate, and evaluation must be distinguished, with reversibility and evaluation central to safe evolution.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL restricts this contract to named scaffold components, binds separate baseline/candidate/evaluation digests, requires zero recorded regressions and bounded metric thresholds, and requires a rollback checkpoint.

features: held-out task and trace evidence binding
quality delta and safety regression thresholds
platform ABI and policy generation binding
explicit approval and bounded canary budget
candidate/canary expiry and request/nonce replay protection

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane admission overhead; excludes deployment, model inference, tools, network, storage, accelerators, kernel scheduling, and human approval latency

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the bounded self-improvement module, tests, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain prior tagged interaction-ledger release

limitations: The ledger evaluates caller-supplied evidence and does not itself run the candidate, generate benchmarks, verify held-out traces, or deploy a canary.
No model weights, privileged kernel code, source tree, production policy, runtime memory, or tools were changed by the contract.
The benchmark measures local Python control-plane overhead and excludes deployment, model, tool, network, storage, accelerator, kernel scheduler, and approval latency.
The real-task validation is a deterministic local fixture and does not establish autonomous learning, general intelligence, model improvement, browser autonomy, robotics, or production efficacy.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or independent external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, or superiority to Linux.
